channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Togo's Prime Minister arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Plus meeting and World Nomad Games
item.description: Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, Chairman of the Council of Ministers of Togo, has arrived in Kyrgyzstan for a working visit. He will attend the SCO Plus meeting and the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games. Kyrgyzstan currently holds the chairmanship of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation.

item.title: Singer Nicole Scherzinger arrives in Kyrgyzstan for World Nomad Games opening ceremony
item.description: American singer Nicole Scherzinger has arrived in Kyrgyzstan to perform at the opening ceremony of the VI World Nomad Games in Bishkek. She was welcomed at Manas International Airport and is scheduled to perform at the Bishkek Arena.

item.title: Xi Jinping Praises Kyrgyzstan's Development, Pledges Deeper Cooperation
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping met with Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov in Bishkek, noting the country's rapid development over seven years. Xi expressed China's readiness to deepen cooperation in various fields, highlighting the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway as a key joint project contributing to regional peace and prosperity.

item.title: First direct flight from Dushanbe to Minsk welcomed in Belarus
item.description: The first direct flight from Dushanbe to Minsk, operated by Somon Air, was welcomed with a traditional water arch ceremony at Minsk National Airport. The new route marks a significant step in strengthening relations and cooperation between Tajikistan and Belarus.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan-China cooperation enters new 'golden period', says President Japarov
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov stated that Kyrgyzstan-China relations have reached a historically high level, entering a new 'golden period' of development. He emphasized the significance of Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit for strengthening friendship and strategic partnership.

item.title: Kabul: Afghanistan poses no threat to neighboring countries, says official
item.description: Afghanistan does not pose a threat to its neighbors, and regional concerns are largely unfounded, stated official representative Zabihullah Mujahid. He suggested that intelligence agencies of hostile countries might be supplying false information to the CSTO. Mujahid affirmed that Afghan security forces fully control the country's borders.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Speaker: President will not surrender powers during election campaign
item.description: The President of Kyrgyzstan will not temporarily relinquish his powers while running for office, stated Parliament Speaker Marlen Mamataliev. Current laws do not require a temporary suspension of duties for a presidential candidate. Mamataliev clarified that all branches of government will continue to function normally, dispelling speculation about him potentially acting as interim president.

item.title: Uzbekistan SSR targeted for 4,750 executions and imprisonments during Great Purge
item.description: According to NKVD data, Central Asia was slated for the repression of 224,400 individuals. The Uzbek SSR was assigned a quota of 4,750 people, comprising 750 for execution and 4,000 for imprisonment.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon travels to Bishkek for SCO Summit
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon departed for Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit of heads of state. He was seen off by high-ranking officials at Dushanbe International Airport.

item.title: Kazakhstan's mining companies can adjust procurement costs due to weak tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Industry and Construction permits solid mineral extraction companies to recalculate procurement costs based on the tenge's exchange rate. This allows adjustments before contract signing or during payment.

item.title: Russia's Defense Ministry announces preparation for massive strikes on Ukraine's energy sector
item.description: The Russian Defense Ministry stated on August 30 that armed forces are preparing new massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities. These actions are described as a response to ongoing Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure and its fuel and energy complex. This announcement follows reports of damage to Russian energy infrastructure from Ukrainian drone attacks.

item.title: Kazakhstan spent billions on energy network repairs, but wear and tear remains high
item.description: Kazakhstan allocated 384 billion tenge for energy infrastructure repairs in 2026, a 9% increase from the previous year. Despite these investments, the wear and tear on networks is expected to decrease by only a few percent. Repairs on power plants and transmission lines are progressing, but heat networks lag behind schedule.

item.title: UN Resident Coordinator reflects on two years in Uzbekistan, climate change, and water reforms
item.description: Akiko Fujii, the UN Resident Coordinator in Uzbekistan, reflects on her two years in the country, noting the significance of the end of the 'chilla' heatwave. She highlights climate change impacts, with over 25% of Uzbekistan's land degraded and 45% at risk of desertification. Recent water code adoption and reforms are seen as positive steps.

item.title: Olzhas Bektenov Reappointed as Prime Minister of Kazakhstan
item.description: Olzhas Bektenov has been reappointed as the Prime Minister of Kazakhstan by the Kurultai, chaired by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Bektenov, who has held the position since 2024, expressed gratitude for the trust and emphasized supporting the president's modernization initiatives as a new stage for the country.

item.title: Number of Entrepreneurs Grows in Tajikistan
item.description: The number of business entities in Tajikistan increased by 4.3% to over 391,000 as of July 1, 2026, according to the State Committee on Investments. Loans to entrepreneurs also rose by 7.4% in the first half of 2026, totaling over 6.3 billion somoni.

item.title: Erlan Karin Appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan
item.description: Former State Secretary Erlan Karin has been appointed Vice President of Kazakhstan by the Kurultai, following a proposal from President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. Karin expressed gratitude and pledged to faithfully fulfill his duties and serve the country.

item.title: US Strikes Iran, Tehran Targets US Bases in Jordan
item.description: US forces attacked missile launch sites on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on August 30. In response, Iran launched missile strikes against US military bases in Jordan, specifically the King Hussein and Al-Azraq bases.

item.title: SCO Humanitarian Event Held in Bishkek Ahead of 2026 Summit
item.description: A Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) humanitarian event, organized by China Media Group and Kyrgyzstan's National Television and Radio Broadcasting Corporation, took place in Bishkek on August 30. Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov sent a congratulatory message, emphasizing the media's role in strengthening SCO understanding.

item.title: Documentary 'In the Name of the Future: Towards the 25th Anniversary of the SCO' Released
item.description: The documentary 'In the Name of the Future: Towards the 25th Anniversary of the SCO' highlights the achievements and significance of multilateral cooperation within the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation. It explores themes like artificial intelligence, infrastructure, agriculture, environmental protection, and humanitarian exchanges.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Decriminalizing Personal Drug Possession
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs proposes shifting responsibility for possession, acquisition, transport, manufacture, and consumption of small amounts of drugs for personal use from criminal to administrative offense. Criminal liability will remain for drug trafficking, production for sale, and large quantities. This reform aims to reduce the number of criminal cases that are later dropped.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Appoints New Ambassador to Tajikistan
item.description: Nazarali Aripov has been appointed as the new Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Kyrgyzstan to Tajikistan. The decree was signed by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Aripov replaces Erlan Abdildaev, who was previously released from this post and appointed Ambassador to Hungary.

item.title: UN Secretary-General António Guterres Arrives in Kyrgyzstan for SCO Summit
item.description: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has arrived in Kyrgyzstan to participate in the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit. He was welcomed at Manas International Airport by the Minister of Economy and Commerce, Bakyt Sydykov. Guterres will attend the Council of Heads of State meeting in Bishkek.

item.title: 12 Uzbek children without parental care returned from Russia
item.description: Twelve underage Uzbek citizens, deprived of parental care or in difficult social situations, have been returned to Uzbekistan from various regions of Russia. The repatriation was a collaborative effort involving the Uzbek embassy, ministries of internal affairs and health, and the National Agency for Social Protection. This year, 38 children have been repatriated from Russia.

item.title: Uzbek President congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev congratulated Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day. Mirziyoyev noted Kyrgyzstan's economic and social growth under Japarov's leadership and highlighted the elevated bilateral relations to a "union level." He also emphasized the importance of regional cooperation and upcoming events.

item.title: Hong Kong banks may finance Tashkent-Samarkand toll road project
item.description: Hong Kong banks are considering financing the construction of the Tashkent-Samarkand toll road. The potential involvement of Hong Kong financial institutions was discussed by Uzbekistan's Transport Minister Ilkhom Makhkamov and the head of Hong Kong's "Belt and Road" Office, Nicholas Ho Lik-chi. Prospects for air travel and economic cooperation were also discussed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Parliament Speaker congratulates nation on Independence Day
item.description: Marlen Mamataliev, Speaker of the Jogorku Kenesh, congratulated Kyrgyzstan's citizens on the 35th anniversary of Independence. He emphasized that strengthening independence is a duty and highlighted the country's progress in economic, state, and international spheres under President Sadyr Japarov. The Speaker wished for peace, unity, and prosperity.

item.title: Kyrgyz State Secretary Links Xi Jinping's Visit to Ancient Monk's Journey
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's State Secretary Arslan Koichiev drew a historical parallel between Xi Jinping's visit and the 7th-century monk Xuanzang's journey. Koichiev noted Xi's visit to the same location Xuanzang stayed and referenced Xi's article on Kyrgyzstan-China relations, highlighting historical figures who fostered cultural exchange.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Asked US to Lead Anti-Houthi War, Washington Refused
item.description: Saudi Arabia requested the United States to lead a war against the Houthis, but Washington declined. This issue was raised during a meeting between Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Admiral Brad Cooper, head of the US Central Command, on August 14.

item.title: US President Trump Congratulates Kyrgyzstan on Independence Day
item.description: US President Donald Trump sent congratulations to Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and the people of Kyrgyzstan on their Independence Day. He highlighted the strong relationship built on mutual respect, economic ties, and shared commitment to regional security. The US reaffirms its support for Kyrgyzstan's sovereignty and independence.

item.title: Leaders of Several Countries Congratulate Kyrgyzstan on 35th Independence Anniversary
item.description: Heads of state from Saudi Arabia, Morocco, Belgium, Iran, Pakistan, Egypt, Belarus, Azerbaijan, and Turkey, along with Armenia's Prime Minister, congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its 35th Independence Day. They wished the nation peace and prosperity and President Japarov good health and success. Several leaders expressed eagerness to deepen bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh President: Kyrgyzstan Has Successfully Developed Since Independence
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev congratulated Kyrgyzstan on its Independence Day, noting its growing authority, evidenced by its UN Security Council election. He highlighted reforms for economic growth and praised the fraternal relations between Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

item.title: Shanghai Cooperation Organization Celebrates 25 Years, Drives Regional Economic Cooperation
item.description: The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) marks its 25th anniversary, having grown into a major international body with 27 member states and a GDP nearing $30 trillion. The SCO actively promotes trade, energy, transport, and digital economy projects, enhancing regional stability and global governance.

item.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Arrives in Bishkek for State Visit and SCO Summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife were welcomed in Bishkek by Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov. Xi Jinping conveyed greetings to the Kyrgyz people, highlighting the long-standing friendship and stable development of bilateral relations, now at a high level of comprehensive partnership.

item.title: Britain warns companies supplying arms to Ukraine about Russian attack risks
item.description: British government officials have informed defense company leaders about increased threats from the Kremlin against them and their staff. This warning comes as companies supply arms to Ukraine, highlighting potential Russian attack risks.

item.title: US strikes Iran's Larak Island; Iran retaliates against US bases in Jordan
item.description: The US conducted strikes on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, targeting forces preparing to mine the strait. Iran's IRGC claimed to have retaliated by striking two US military bases in Jordan, targeting infrastructure and fighter jets.

item.title: New Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway shows significant damage after construction
item.description: Activists report significant damage to the new Taldykorgan-Ust-Kamenogorsk highway, including asphalt degradation and foundation issues, less than two years after its completion. The road, built with Chinese loans, cost over 180 billion tenge and has a two-year warranty.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India Elevate Strategic Partnership to New Level
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Uzbekistan on August 29-30 for a state visit. Discussions focused on deepening strategic partnership and multifaceted cooperation. Trade turnover exceeded $1 billion last year, and the number of joint ventures has increased sevenfold.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses SCO Summit on Economic Cooperation and Infrastructure
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will attend the SCO summit in Bishkek on August 31-September 1. The summit marks the organization's 25th anniversary and aims to advance economic, transport, and anti-crisis agendas. Leaders from 21 countries, including China, Russia, and India, are expected to participate.

item.title: Indian Prime Minister's State Visit to Uzbekistan Concludes with Signed Agreements
item.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi concluded his state visit to Uzbekistan on August 29-30. High-level talks focused on deepening strategic partnership and cooperation in trade, energy, health, and other sectors. A significant package of bilateral agreements was signed.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India aim to reach $5 billion trade volume by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan and India have agreed to increase their trade turnover to $5 billion by 2030. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit Bishkek for the SCO summit and the World Nomad Games.
